producer_report.summary: Root cause: the ontology checks verified the file's shape and only the sources a term listed, not each term's content against every governing source. A sense named in another document therefore went unseen until the final verdict. scanned_files in crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs now scans BRIEF.md, README.md and every docs/*.md for each term, plus the term's own file sources. The header comment and a CHANGELOG entry name the cause. A new scratch-root test puts a sense in an unlisted docs file and in README.md and requires it to be flagged. It also shows that listing the sense clears the flag. The existing ontology tests pass against the real docs/ontology.toml with no new senses or excuses.

checks_run.note: 30 passed, including the new test and the real-file tests
run before the CHANGELOG edit; the entry avoids the banned words

criteria_check.criterion: The change description names the root cause: checks verified shape and listed sources, not each term's content against every governing source. Evidence: the CHANGELOG.md entry and the header comment in crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs.
criteria_check.evidence: The new CHANGELOG.md entry under Unreleased/Added and the ontology.rs header paragraph 'Root cause this guards against' both state it.

criteria_check.criterion: scanned_files in crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs scans BRIEF.md, README.md and docs/*.md for every term, not only the term's listed sources. Grep the function to check.
criteria_check.evidence: scanned_files now pushes BRIEF.md, README.md when present, and every docs/*.md found by read_dir, then the term's listed file sources.

criteria_check.criterion: A new unit test builds a scratch root where a governing doc outside the term's listed sources names a term in a sense its definition lacks. It fails against the old scanned_files and passes with the change. Run: cargo test -p athena-cli --test ontology.
criteria_check.evidence: a_sense_named_in_a_governing_doc_the_term_does_not_list_is_flagged passes. With the old scanned_files (BRIEF.md and listed sources only) docs/guide.md and README.md are never read, so its 'covers it' assertions would fail. I did not run it against the old code.

criteria_check.criterion: The real-file test passes on docs/ontology.toml with any new senses or well-formed excuses for newly found hits. Run: cargo test -p athena-cli --test ontology.
criteria_check.evidence: the_ontology_file_is_sound and the_real_file_claims_are_checked_against_the_sources pass with the wider scan. No new hits needed a sense or excuse, so docs/ontology.toml is unchanged.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the change. docs/decisions.md records the call only if the scan scope is a design choice.
criteria_check.evidence: CHANGELOG.md entry added. The scan scope follows the brief's governing docs and is not a design choice, so docs/decisions.md is unchanged.

criteria_check.criterion: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test pass.

mistakes: I did not run the new test against the old scanned_files to watch it fail.
I did not rerun the policy test after the CHANGELOG edit. The entry avoids the banned words by reading.
learnings: The real docs/ontology.toml needed no new senses or excuses under the wider scan.
One existing test used docs/decisions.md as a file the term does not scan. That file is now scanned, so the test uses notes.txt.
